items.content:
Gaming Garena’s Palworld Online Release Date Leaked Last Word on Gaming Arijit Das Wed, September 2, 2026 at 12:08 PM UTC Wed, September 2, 2026 at 12:08 PM UTC The Palworld Online release date has been leaked, and Garena's MMORPG adventure game is now expected to be released later this year.

With an official licence from Pocketpair, Garena first announced Palworld Online for iOS and Android on 3rd August, 2026. The announcement came shortly after Palworld 1.0 Full Release.

On 1st September 2026, Garena officially announced Palworld Online pre-registration for Android and iOS in South Korea.

The pre-registration announcement came alongside a gameplay trailer that shared a glimpse of Palworld Online's combat, exploration, and other features.

Shortly after the pre-registration for Palworld Online went live, a Palworld Online release date quickly went viral in the gaming community.

Players who went on to pre-register for Palworld Online on their iOS devices saw a Palworld Online release date being showcased in the App Store.

As per the App Store, Palworld Online is set to release on 30th November 2026. We have yet to receive any statement from Garena regarding the official release date of Palworld Online.

In addition to the expected Palworld Online release date, we have received the device requirements for the game.

As per @DramicGaming on X , the base size of the game is 2.9 GB. It requires iOS 12.0 or later for iPhone, iPad, and iPod Touch.

There are Palworld Online pre-registration rewards available for players. Players can expect 50,000 Gold Coins, 20 Training Manuals (M), 50 Dog Coins, a Huge Verdant Egg, and 10 Tera Spheres based on the number of pre-registrations.

Moreover, special bonus items for all pre-registered players will be officially announced by Garena at a later date.

items.content:
Garena announced on the 2nd that it has opened domestic pre-registration for the mobile multiplayer RPG 'Palworld Online'.

'Palworld Online' is a new title developed and published by Garena based on an official license from Japanese game developer Pocketpair. It utilizes the 'Palworld' IP, which has accumulated over 40 million players worldwide, and is scheduled to launch first globally in Korea in 2026.

The game is designed around player cooperation and shared growth. It features cooperative Pal-capturing gameplay, PvE content, PvP combat, and shared base management. Core elements of the original title—such as Pal collecting, survival, crafting, and open-world exploration—have also been implemented in a seamless online world tailored for mobile environments.

Players can explore the open world with other players, build structures, and engage in combat.

Pre-registration is available on Google Play and the Apple App Store. Depending on the number of participants, rewards such as 50,000 Gold Coins, 20 Training Manuals (M), 50 Dog Coins, a Huge Verdant Egg, and 10 Tera Spheres will be distributed, while rewards for all pre-registered users will be revealed at a later date.

items.summary: Looking for a list of every Pal in Palworld? Palworld is all about exploring the vast map and discovering new Pals. As you would expect, it'll take a
items.content:
Looking for a list of every Pal in Palworld ? Palworld is all about exploring the vast map and discovering new Pals. As you would expect, it'll take a while to collect the full Palpedia, so if you're wondering which Pals you're still missing, or which Pals offer the best work suitability traits for your base, this (in-progress!) Palpedia guide will help you out.

There are currently 287 Pals in Palworld. 137 were released at launch, 2 as part of the Raid Update; 24 arrived in the Sakurajima update; and another 24 came out as part of the Feybreak Island update. Version 1.0 added a full 73 additional Pals in total, as well as reshuffling their numbers in the Palpedia.

In addition, Version 1.0 did a general balance pass on many Pals, which changed their partner skills, work suitabilities, food consumption, and other relevant stats. If you're coming back to Palworld with a save from Early Access, many of your go-to strategies and base setups may no longer apply, or may not be as efficient as they used to be.

Most of the Pals in Palworld drop something upon their defeat, whether they're incapacitated through damage or captured in a Sphere. The drops listed below for every Pal are for standard, open-world encounters.

You can also encounter an "Alpha" version of almost any Pal inside one of Palworld's randomly generated dungeons, while a few dozen more are fixed encounters in the overworld. These Alpha Pals have their own drop table, which includes the standard Pal's items plus a few rarer reagents. Almost all Alpha Pals will drop vendor items (Rubies, Precious Pelts, etc.) and Ancient Civilization Parts, along with a very slim chance to drop common-quality accessories.

Listed by their Palpedia entry number, here's an overview of all the Pals in Palworld.

There is a rare variant of Gumoss that can be found in the wild with a flower on its head, which has a low chance to appear in place of the standard version. If defeated, it drops Beautiful Flowers in addition to its other items. As far as the Palpedia is concerned, however, it's the same ol' Gumoss.

Sometimes produces Flame Organ when assigned to Ranch.

Increases the efficiency of destroying Stone by 500% while the player is riding Rushoar, making mining significantly faster.

Higher levels of partner skill increase the glide speed and lowers the rate of descent.

While mounted on Elkthyrdeer, the player's Lumbering efficiency improves by 220%, speeding up the process of cutting down trees.

While fighting together, Sweepa's Attack and Defense increase by 0 to 8% for every Swee on your team, based on Sweepa's partner skill level.

Any Ground Pals in your party receive a 10% to 20% Attack boost.

Higher levels of Hangyu's partner skill also lower Stamina loss from gliding and lower the rate at which gravity influences the player while gliding.

items.title: Palworld TCG developers apologize as the game sells out across retailers amidst higher-than-anticipated demand
items.summary: Bushiroad has also announced anti-scalping measures like selling packages with the shrink wrap removed in Japan.
items.content:
Home News Palworld TCG developers apologize as the game sells out across retailers amidst higher-than-anticipated demand Bushiroad has also announced anti-scalping measures like selling packages with the shrink wrap removed in Japan.

News 2026-08-14 17:45 Amber V Bushiroad launched the Palworld Official Card Game and its first booster pack “Dawn of Palpagos” on July 30. Based on Pocketpair’s hit monster-taming survival game, the TCG sold over 3.5 million packs worldwide just via pre-orders, and has been selling out at retailers as well amidst higher-than-expected demand.

In a statement from August 12, Bushiroad’s Japanese account acknowledged that there has been a “continued shortage of stock,” apologizing to fans who aren’t able to buy the game. The company is currently discussing measures internally in order to get the Palworld TCG into the hands of as many people as possible.

Regarding the Japanese version of Dawn of Palpagos, which was likewise sold out, Bushiroad announced a new shipment set to arrive on the evening of August 14 at pop-up stores. It has also announced that boxes will be sold with the shrink wrap removed, most likely as a countermeasure against scalpers.

items.content:
\

Palworld version v1.0.3 has been released!

＝＝＝

\

▼Items and Equipment ・Changed the unlock level of some Jetragon-related technologies from 79 to 70, and reduced the materials required for the Pal Gear used to ride Jetragon.

・Changed the technology unlock level of the Aquatic Construction Kit from Level 66 to Level 23, changed its Ancient Technology Point requirement from 4 to 1, and adjusted the required materials and work amount.

・Extended the duration of World Tree Holy Water.

・Reduced the weight of World Tree Holy Water from 1 to 0.1.

・Added World Tree Holy Water to the rewards for World Tree expeditions, World Tree fishing, and the Large Fishing Pond.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Pals in The World Tree area.

・Increased the amount of World Tree Holy Water obtained from Teafant Spring.

・Adjusted the work amount required to craft the Ancient Armor series.

・Doubled the amount of Fiber obtained from trees.

▼Bases and Missions

・Reduced the building costs of the Crude Oil Extractor, High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor, and Large Power Generator.

・Increased the crude oil production speed of the Crude Oil Extractor and High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

・The base mission that requires building a Crude Oil Extractor can now also be progressed by building a High-Pressure Crude Oil Extractor.

▼Server Settings

・Added a server setting (bAllowEnemyCampSpawnNearBaseCamp) that disables the suppression of enemy camp spawns near player base camps.

\

▼Graphics and Display

・Adjusted the boundary display in some areas to make it easier to see from a distance.

・Improved the display quality of some objects in dungeons.

▼Sound

・Added a sound effect when using World Tree Holy Water.

\

▼Crashes and Progression Blockers

・Fixed an issue where the mission could become impossible to progress if the barrier was removed before accepting the main mission in Sunreach.

▼Multiplayer and Co-op

・Fixed an issue in co-op where lighting on the client side could display incorrectly after cutscenes or the ending played.

・Fixed an issue in co-op where some scenes could stutter during the cutscene that plays when entering The World Tree.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Fast Travel could activate unintentionally during Tower Boss battles.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where Pals could appear to vibrate rapidly on the client screen.

▼Pals and NPCs

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop fighting.

・Fixed an issue where the summoned Pal could stop helping with base work.

・Fixed an issue in multiplayer where, when the Partner Skill of Orserk or certain other Pals activated, the effect display could fail to update correctly, making it appear as though the skill had not activated.

・Fixed an issue where Alpha Surfent would not produce Leather when assigned to a Ranch.

▼Battles and Bosses

・Fixed an issue where some raid boss battles could fail to progress as intended.

・Fixed an issue where the wave effect and actual damage range did not match for some of Panthalus's attacks.

▼Bases and Building

・Fixed an issue where the placement detection for stairs and slanted roofs could fail to match their actual shape.

・Fixed an issue where stairs could not be placed correctly on the sides of foundations or roofs.

▼Items and Rewards

・Fixed an issue where the reward settings for the normal Moon Lord battle and the Ultra Raid Boss battle had not been updated to the intended settings.

・Fixed an issue where items could duplicate when performing certain actions.

・Fixed an issue where, when Katress's Partner Skill activated, switching spheres while riding could allow the player to obtain a different type of sphere.

・Fixed an issue where the World Tree Holy Water effect did not display correctly on the Pal being ridden when using World Tree Holy Water while riding.

・Fixed an issue where, after the World Tree Holy Water effect ended, riding a Pal would cause the World Tree Holy Water aura to reappear and not disappear when approaching trees in The World Tree area.

・Fixed an issue where an unintended reward was set for the desert expedition.

・Fixed an issue where the Dark Skill Fruit: Psycho Gravity did not appear on the item search screen.

・Fixed a bug where the firing interval was not set for sphere launchers

▼UI, Display, and Text

・Fixed an issue where resolution settings would not apply correctly in fullscreen mode.

・Fixed an issue where, after switching window mode with F11 / Alt+Enter, the game could unintentionally return to fullscreen mode after loading.

・Fixed an issue where, if certain effects were on screen while aiming, the entire screen could become blurred.

▼Sound

・Fixed an issue where the water sound effect could fail to play at Teafant Spring.

・Fixed an issue on dedicated servers where the BGM for Attack Choppers triggered by other players could play even from far away.

・Adjusted the BGM playback range for Attack Choppers so that it plays correctly for players who are Wanted.

・Fixed an issue where unintended footstep sounds could play when walking on furniture or facilities.

▼Controls

・Fixed an issue where, after changing the key assignment for ""Attack that enemy!"" in Controls, selecting ""Restore to Default"" would not restore the default setting.

・Fixed an issue where settings could be applied unintentionally when interacting with the change confirmation dialog and duplicate key warning in Controls.

▼Map and Exploration

・Fixed an issue where a beach-like display could remain on the water surface after Fast Traveling to an offshore base.

＝＝＝

Thank you for your continued support of Palworld.

▼Controls

・Fixed an issue where, when carrying over settings from versions earlier than v0.7, changes unrelated to Controls could still be treated as control setting conflicts.

・Fixed an issue where the Inventory Shortcut option was not displayed in Controls.

▼UI

・Fixed an issue where the damage number displayed when destroying ore while mining could sometimes appear as 0.

▼Performance Improvements

items.title: Palworld 1.0 Review – Bigger, Better, and Still Brutally Addictive
items.summary: Palworld 1.0 is crammed with new content. More Pals, better quests, and a fully realized world for new and returning players to explore.
items.content:
Remember Palworld ? Well, the controversial game from Pocketpair finally has a 1.0 release. After two years, this feels like a very different animal than the one I initially encountered. The quest system is more complete, the UI is polished, and the world feels much more interconnected than before. While there are still some rough edges, this version of Palworld is a vastly improved one.

Now, I haven’t been keeping up with every iteration of Palworld released up to this point. So I’m not clear on how gradual or sudden these changes might be. But oh man, the quest system feels like night and day. You’re fed a steady stream of quests from the jump. They pair nicely with the tech tree, they appear on your map, and they sync with your compass. Yes, this is incredibly basic stuff. We figured out quest design decades ago. But you really appreciate the elegance of that design when it’s missing. Then when it finally shows up? It’s water in the desert.

Beyond the quests, it turns out Palworld works much better with connective tissue in place. Fast travel points, side quests, a detailed map, and distant objectives (like a floating island on the horizon) all make the world feel more tangible. Having an objective at all times kept me hooked on the game. Or at least, objectives are perfect for stringing you along until the factory sim element gets its claws in you. Once the big machine gets going, you don’t need anything else to maintain momentum.

The complete list of additions in Palworld 1.0 is downright intimidating. You can read the whole thing on their Steam page, but the highlights are remarkable. 72 new Pals, the Sunreach region, the World Tree, and an increased level cap all speak to a much larger, more complete game. There’s more of course, but the point remains – Palworld has undergone significant changes since the early access days.

This new version of Palworld still has some flaws, to be fair. The laptop I’m using is decently powerful, but I encountered a handful of framerate dips regardless. More important than the tiny performance issues is the core gameplay loop. Things hum along at a more relatable pace than ever before, sure. But you’re still faced with a pretty murderous grind. Pal levels creep upward slowly, and getting through that tech trees gets daunting quite quickly. While things start out breezy enough, the endgame is strictly for simulation psychopaths.

By which I mean the truly dedicated. Which is totally fine! There’s a fascinating disconnect between the monster battling and the base building. You can immerse yourself in one and ignore the other, at least for a hefty chunk of playtime. Although perhaps my impressions of the battling are skewed by hands off it all is. Your Pals run on autopilot, both in battle and beyond it. So for me, the fights are a diversion from my tiny empire.

In that regard, Palworld remains a specialized interest. Either you’re ready to get lost in the details of empire expansion and monster murder, or you’ll quickly lose momentum. The quest system, new content, and expanded Pal roster are all incidental in the face of this essential truth. The gooey caramel center that is the gameplay loop is more or less the same as it ever was. My mind was changed about this game, true. But I’m prone to hyper focus and bouts of mania. So a vast and ruthless machine like Palworld is straight up catnip for my badly wired brain.

The 1.0 release of Palworld presents a very different game than the original early access version. The quest system has been revamped, the map has been expanded, and civilization is scattered everywhere. But the gameplay loop is still pretty relentless. Plus, the rough edges haven’t been completely removed. If the old game was almost it for you, this new iteration might be exactly what you yearned for. But Palworld 1.0 is still an acquired taste.

***A Steam key was provided by the publisher***
